rows.notes: The cited study is a literature review (Section 2 describes a database search of papers 2009-2019; Figs 1-3 summarise counts of reviewed papers). It reports no data, experiment, survey or model runs of its own. It discusses advanced control (PID, fuzzy, ANN, MPC, adaptive DSS) and feedback architectures as routes to water-use efficiency, but all water-saving results are cited from other work (e.g. Lefkowitz 2019 for 40% saving with predictive model; Tseng et al. 2018 for 52%). Q1 'no' so Q2-Q9 'no'.

Review article, not a primary study. It describes closed-loop controllers conceptually (Section 5.2, Fig. 9) and notes open-loop systems cannot react to varying conditions (Section 5.1, citing Patil and Desai 2013), but presents no own evidence that feedback prevents persistent over- or under-irrigation under uncertainty. Q1 'no' so all other questions 'no'.

Review article with no own data. The paper does not itself show that dependable reductions in excessive irrigation arise from improved timing/amount decisions under uncertainty; it only summarises other studies' claims about water saving from MPC, fuzzy, ANN and IoT-based controllers. Q1 'no' so Q2-Q9 'no'.

Review article, no primary data. The paper frames benefits of precision irrigation as water-use efficiency and water saving (citing others), and does not discuss reallocation of saved water to stabilise production or expand irrigated area at all; the rebound/withdrawal distinction in the passage is not addressed. Q1 'no' so Q2-Q9 'no'.

Review article, no own measurements. It mentions generically that sensors require installation and calibration and are costly (Section 5.2), that TDR sensors are expensive, that PID controllers suffer from disturbances, and that ANN accuracy depends on data quality (Section 5.2.2.2), but reports no own evidence on sensor drift, communication dropouts or incomplete coverage degrading performance or introducing risk. Q1 'no' so Q2-Q9 'no'.

Review article without own experiments. It asserts, drawing on cited literature, that advanced control (MPC, fuzzy, ANN, adaptive DSS) with real-time IoT monitoring can improve water-use efficiency, and that controller performance depends on accurate models/data (Sections 5.2.2-5.2.4), but no own result on reducing excess irrigation. Q1 'no' so Q2-Q9 'no'.

Review article without own experiments. The paper does not evaluate risk management (e.g. avoiding crop water stress) as an outcome of advanced control; it only describes controllers and cites others' findings. The statement that success depends on reliable monitoring and robust logic is a general narrative point, not an own finding. Q1 'no' so Q2-Q9 'no'.

notes: The cited document is a narrative review (Abioye et al., 2020, Computers and Electronics in Agriculture) of monitoring and advanced control strategies for precision irrigation. It contains no primary data; its only own content is a bibliometric summary of selected papers (Figs 1-3) and a conceptual classification of control techniques. All seven claim rows therefore receive Q1 'no' and 'no' for Q2-Q9. Full text appears complete including references.
